recorded_boundaries.text: These are the premises of the universally quantified target, not independently supplied existence results.
This is the setting of the manuscript theorem; it is not a finite-instance algorithmic runtime guarantee.
The diffusion premise belongs to the first two conjuncts of value_consequences. Its final ground-state/Parisi equality has only the minimizer premise.
This records the minimizer premise of the formal interface; it does not assert that a minimizer exists.
The extensive uncut Hamiltonian need not have an operator limit. Smallness of a generator on a core alone is not the needed exponential or domain statement.

The proof first fixes outer Lipschitz constants, then inner errors, using seed truncation, the regularized inverse sine, cutoffs and Fourier approximation. Approximation is in the rooted L² norm, not merely in marginal distribution.
This query root keeps the fixed-minimizer hypothesis in scope and exposes the complete conditional scalar-to-rooted construction. It is not a declaration that a minimizer exists.

Closed witness application: attainment supplies gamma in the manuscript class U, and the universally quantified fixed-minimizer construction uses that same gamma before any finite choices are frozen. Its annotated support edge exposes the conditional argument while discharging the supplied manuscript admissibility and minimizer premises only within this use. The binding is authored source correspondence, not mechanically checked witness equality or proof acceptance.
Disjoint mask orthogonality and the Gaussian isometry control the loss. Shared descendant branches are not assumed independent. Uniform derivative bounds refer to the original grouped coordinates.
Both norm convergence and the occupation bound are hypotheses. Strong convergence or one-point distributional convergence by itself does not permit multiplying an edge correlation by √D.
Equality of seed marginals or ordinary Gram convergence does not alone prove rooted energy convergence. The displayed L-pairing calculation is a separate ingredient.
BFMVZ Theorem 1 is a fixed-depth, fixed-angle identity. It does not transfer raw seeded, masked or controlled words, give a joint n,p,D limit, or certify the construction preceding seed removal.

Measurable seed masks are permitted through bounded subsequences with Gaussian almost-everywhere convergence. Grouped finite control coordinates are essential; no dimension-free assertion is made for all flattened color coordinates.

The receiving root seed is independent of these child fields. The first-chaos identity is an identity in the shared rooted space; a marginal Gaussian law alone does not identify E(v). This is a manuscript construction, not a Lean declaration.

First fix the finite input channels and surrounding word. Helper pinning concerns all helper descendants, not only the receiver root. Individual approximating commutator factors need not preserve that subspace. Lower first responses and scalar second responses must be retained; covariance between channels cannot be discarded.

This is finite approximation of selected local rooted operations. It is not a uniform global operator-norm Trotter estimate on an extensive Hamiltonian, and no error may be multiplied by a growing vertex count.

The finite word and all angles are held fixed before D→∞. Rotated axes and a seed gate exp(−it Zs) have the corresponding rooted formulas; this calculation alone is not a transfer theorem for seeded words.

This is an existence statement for one common finite word. Cost gates, mixers, identity padding and combining adjacent equal gate types convert it to the standard alternating QAOA convention. The tree-to-SK step is still a separate theorem.
The exponential statement has its own domain and weighted Gronwall argument. It is not inferred solely from a small Hilbert–Schmidt kernel or small generator.

This realizes both the finite scalar joint law and its shifted energy pairing. It does not assert strong finite-degree convergence for the unsmoothed sign formula. Intermediate transmitted columns need not be bounded.
The full displaced packets may have occupation of order r^(−2); only their tails have uniform weighted bounds. No uniform whole-packet occupation bound is imported from the finite-word degree limit.

Some ordinary angles are of order 1/r and can be very large, but are finite before any degree or system-size limit. The theorem gives no bound on word length, angle size or an efficient search procedure.

The same vertex seed is reused in every seed gate. Compilation proceeds outer rank to inner rank: pointwise approximants, sender partitions, finite commutators, then lower ranks; raw-seed masks are compiled last. No uniformity as helper probabilities vanish or circuit length grows is claimed.
One must prove the net o(r) cancellation. Replacing a moving insertion by an O(r)-accurate approximation and subsequently multiplying that error by 1/r is not valid.
The word is finite after the projection list is fixed. This is exact finite-list ensemble control of limiting packet data, not a uniform control statement over a continuum of unknown centers.
The order is terminal cutoff, finite scalar mesh, then finite smoothing. The statement has no joint-limit or uniform-in-terminal-time rate and still allows unbounded intermediate columns.

The displacement limit uses the o(r) error and the actual insertion change. Norm remainders are transported through unitaries; an unbounded observable is not applied to an uncontrolled norm remainder.
No maximizer of the noncompact angle supremum is required; no exact optimality at finite depth is inferred.

The construction must not choose a list from its own as-yet-unproved small-r limit. The perturbation preserves the target energy by continuity; it supplies finite nonvanishing conditions, not a uniform numerical lower bound over all words.

Uniformity concerns a fixed finite calculation, bounded parameter sets and specified weighted norms. It does not imply global operator-norm convergence, a nondegenerate covariance assumption, or uniformity in growing word length.

Pure zero-field SK with covariance normalization xi(t)=t^2/2. Conditional on the supplied order parameter being an admissible integrable minimizer; no separate assertion that a minimizer exists. FullSupportConclusion includes Stieltjes-measure and diffusion existence, full relative support, strict increase, and the two selected diffusion moment identities. It does not assert QAOA circuit-energy convergence.

Pure zero-field SK with covariance normalization xi(t)=t^2/2. Conditional on the supplied order parameter being an admissible integrable minimizer; no separate assertion that a minimizer exists. FullSupportConclusion includes Stieltjes-measure and diffusion existence, full relative support, strict increase, and the two selected diffusion moment identities. It does not assert QAOA circuit-energy convergence.

The first two conjuncts are conditional on IsMinimizer and IsDiffusion; the final Parisi-value equality needs IsMinimizer. These are scalar ground-state value and finite Gaussian approximation statements. They do not assert QAOA circuit-energy convergence or an efficient angle-selection algorithm.

Manuscript-level claim with system size tending to infinity first and circuit depth then increasing; finite deterministic angles depend on the desired accuracy and are independent of system size and disorder. No quantitative finite-size estimate, depth bound, or efficient angle-selection procedure is claimed. The whole manuscript argument has not been independently reviewed here and has no retained Lean circuit-convergence target.
This is a conditional expectation identity, not a claim that F_N equals the terminal gradient pointwise. Independence and the bound |u|≤1 are essential.
Control is in growing-dimensional ell², not only coordinatewise. The rounding-coordinate boundary term A_N B_{N+1} is retained until shown to vanish.
T is fixed first. Normalizers are eventually positive uniformly over active indices, not asserted positive for all meshes. The g_j have no sqrt(Δ) factor; that factor enters M_N=∑sqrt(Δ)g_j/c_j.

The sum is shifted: B_{j+1}, including the final rounding coordinate. N is mesh count, distinct from spin-system size n. No circuit, efficient computation, convergence rate, uniform terminal estimate, or prescribed diagonal N(T) is supplied by this proposition.

Additional moment-bootstrap and fixed-time flattening argument. Not part of FullSupportConclusion and not needed by the QAOA scalar construction; do not place it in that prerequisite closure. The numerical lower bound is an ordinary deduction in long §9.2, not an extra clause of the selected formal endpoint; it depends on the same minimizer and moment normalization.

An ordinary one-dimensional calculus lemma with its own quantified hypotheses. It applies to toy curves as well as diffusion moments and carries no minimizer, PDE or stochastic premise. Strict convexity gives q′(t) below its endpoint chord for r<t<s; the chord is at most one, and continuity makes the integrated deficit strictly positive. The source uses this step inside a conditional full-support argument. This node does not assert a newly extracted Lean declaration or independently accepted formal check.

The cited Lean declaration records a sampled chord limit and the resulting variational inequality; it is not asserted to have the identical type. A coefficient-convexity/Lipschitz bridge can relate these analytic statements, but no new Lean theorem is claimed.

Authored fixed-time consequence of smooth finite-step coercivity and compact-strip spatial-moment convergence. The ordinary proof flattens gamma locally; the inspected SKSupport source instead uses sampled jets along its canonical diffusion. actual_coercivity takes t:Time with 0<t and ContinuousAt gamma.val t and proves the scaled c^4/c^2 polynomial inequality. Its type does not require c>0; positivity is needed here to divide by c^2. This source correspondence does not identify the SKSupport and SKValue models, pass third time derivatives through a shrinking-plateau limit, or establish the smooth-density corollary as an exported formal conclusion. No fresh Lean build, elaborated dependency extraction, Comparator result or independent semantic acceptance is recorded.

support_boundary.meaning: Not mapped as a claim means absent from the selected passages' claim_ids, not absent from their prose. Explicit assumption references and all recorded prerequisites are retained. No sentence-level explanation coverage is inferred.

paper_scope.meaning: Authored focus; mentioned claims and retained prerequisites may extend beyond these goals.

coverage.heading_syntax: ATX headings only; Setext and HTML headings are not parsed
coverage.scope: Mapped passages are correspondences, not sentence-level formal support. Section-passage overlaps are document structure, not claim or proof implications. Unmapped text and passages omitted by the selector remain in the validated paper. Graph records outside the selected prerequisite closure remain in the bundle and are not asserted absent. Argument links combine recorded Lean references, curated support, formalization correspondence and explicit assumptions; their SCCs describe only that mixed recorded reachability. Reading order and platform decomposition are separate.

passages.text:
The full-support manuscript proves that an admissible integrable minimizer
of the zero-temperature Parisi functional for the pure zero-field
Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model has Stieltjes support equal to every overlap
scale in [0,1). The proof turns a hypothetical support gap into a constant
interval for the order parameter. Variational contact at the ends of that
interval conflicts with a strict curvature inequality inside it. Along the
auxiliary diffusion, the spatial gradient of the value function is a bounded
martingale. Full support makes this martingale's second moment equal to time;
its terminal correlation with Brownian motion gives the ground-state value.
The manuscript's further argument gives a smooth Stieltjes density, strictly
positive on $(0,1)$, and no atom at zero. Sections 9.1–9.2 derive this stronger
ordinary conclusion separately from the selected formal support statement.

This record reconstructs those arguments and follows the finite Gaussian
approximation into the separate QAOA manuscript. The latter claims that
finite deterministic circuits approach the SK optimum when system size tends
to infinity before circuit depth increases. Its circuit construction needs
additional approximation, synthesis, seed-removal and transfer arguments.
The two formal statements concern full support and scalar value
consequences; neither states QAOA circuit convergence. Their verification
scope is described at the end. See [OpenAI (2026a), §§1–2][fs-main] and
[OpenAI (2026b), Theorem 1.1][q-intro].

at a spin-valued random variable whose Brownian correlation represents

fixed $T<1$, followed by $T\uparrow1$. Its formal statement is separate
and retains the minimizer and diffusion hypotheses where needed. The QAOA
theorem goes further: for each requested accuracy it selects one finite
deterministic circuit, independent of size and disorder, whose limiting
expected energy approaches $P_*$. Neither formal statement asserts that
circuit conclusion.

passages.text: ### 10.1 Contact from convexity on constant intervals There is a second way to obtain $q=t$ from the variational inequalities. It uses convexity on intervals where the tail potential is positive, rather than first proving full Stieltjes support. This is the argument used by the scalar implementation; it does not depend on the formal full-support theorem. In the scalar model put $q(t)=\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]$, $f(t)=q(t)-t$ and $G(t)=\int_t^1f(s)\,ds$. The source first obtains $G\ge0$, $G(1)=0$, $q(0)=0$ and $G'=-f$. Compact-mass variations also show that on any interval where $G>0$ the coefficient is constant: if its cumulative mass increased between two points there, integration of the strictly positive $G$ against that positive increment would contradict the mass-removal variational inequality. This is the content of the [scalar contact-integral argument][scalar-contact-integral]. Suppose now that $G(x)>0$ for some $00$, and $q(0)=0$ when $a=0$. If $c>0$, one also has $G(a)=0$. The only extra case is $a=0$: right continuity gives $\gamma(0)=c>0$, so the mass-removal condition at that initial atom forces $G(0)=0$. The mean-value theorem on $[a,x]$ and $[x,b]$ now provides points $r0$; the same right-endpoint argument produces $z>s$ with $f(z)\le f(s)$. Since $f(a)=0$, $$ \frac{f(s)-f(a)}{s-a}>0\ge \frac{f(z)-f(s)}{z-s}, $$ contradicting monotonicity of adjacent secant slopes of a convex function. This case does not need $G(a)=0$; see [the zero-coefficient hump lemma][scalar-zero-hump]. Thus $G$ cannot have a positive component, and $G\equiv0$ on $(0,1)$. Differentiation gives $q(t)=t$ there, with the origin supplied separately. The [scalar assembly][scalar-contact-assembly] then obtains the unit curvature moment, finite Gaussian approximation and terminal value identities from this contact equality. Nonstrict convexity suffices for this scalar route. The strict curvature estimate in Sections 4–5 has the further job of excluding gaps in Stieltjes support. These are source-level proof reconstructions, not a fresh Lean acceptance or a claim that the two formal models have been composed.

The full-support theorem and scalar-value theorem use related but
different formal representations. Their mathematical conclusions can be
discussed together, but a direct formal implication would require the
coefficient, Brownian law, control value and diffusion translations
described in §12, with common witnesses. The finite Gaussian result
also needs its rooted energy identification before it says anything
about a QAOA circuit. The boundedness, regularization, synthesis and
transfer estimates in §8 are additional steps, with temperature-specific
hypotheses where the positive-temperature route is used.

Infinite support allows gaps. An indefinite curvature identity does not imply
strict convexity before expectation is controlled. An algebraic certificate
does not establish its analytic hypotheses. Coordinatewise convergence does
not control a growing coefficient sum. A finite-dimensional Gaussian law
does not identify an energy observable without its operator argument.
Separate witnesses cannot be merged silently. The order
$\forall\varepsilon\ \exists\text{finite word}\ \lim_{n\to\infty}$
cannot be replaced by a fixed-instance depth limit.

The local comparison in §11.1 concerns two printed finite-step displays;
it neither replaces the cited theorem's hypotheses nor supplies the
remaining circuit estimates.

their implementations and build metadata. The derived project specifies

Theorem Prover and Programming Language*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-79876-5_37)
and [The mathlib Community (2020), *The Lean Mathematical Library*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3372885.3373824).
These references credit the software; the retained project metadata identifies
the versions used for this source. The retained polynomial computation
in §4 uses exact rational arithmetic. Its expansion matches
all 22 positive remainder
coefficients. The surplus of the $v^4$ coefficient above $1/1000$ is
$140507/1521000000$. This finite check does not establish the PDE
signs, integrability, boundary flux or limiting argument.

The source-byte audit verified the inspected edition; it did not prove
its claims. Paper assembly checked identifiers, declared scope and
document bindings, not semantic correspondence or reader understanding.
Tool-compatibility checks and synthetic fixtures exercised their stated
cases, not either selected SK theorem. Reading of the mathematical and
formal sources supports the bounded comparisons reported here, without
a complete independent proof acceptance or transitive axiom audit.

The retained observations must be kept separate. The original graph records
unrun plans and an earlier full-support attempt that could not start
because the Comparator executable was unavailable. A later retained
attempt, observed on 23 October 2026, built and exported the challenge,
then stopped while building the implementing solution. The retained
partial-observation receipt and log preserve that event: the imported
object for `Diffusion/AbsIncrement` was missing. The challenge is an
admitted specification, so its successful build and export are not a
proof of the theorem. There was no successful solution export or
research-target comparison in that observation.

The scalar-value invocation in the same original two-target run reached
a terminal failure observed on 24 October 2026. Its challenge built and
exported, but its solution build stopped because the imported object for
`Gaussian/IntegralPositiveMulGaussian` was missing. The retained scalar
receipt and log establish no solution export, kernel acceptance or
comparison acceptance. The companion source review locates both records.
Both failures concern the original build configuration. A subsequent
repair to the derived configuration was recorded. In the subsequent
corrected replay, the full-support challenge built and its exporter was
observed running. Reconciliation on 25 October found that the controller
had stopped without a recovered terminal research result. Comparator
and research extraction outcomes therefore remain unknown, neither
rejected nor accepted. The companion source review retains this
interruption separately from the original build failures.

The later observation is additional run history, not a replacement for
the earlier event or a mathematical rejection of the theorem. Neither
research target has a successful source-bound comparison and transitive
axiom audit established here. Permitted axioms and checker settings
describe configuration; source names and tool-fixture receipts cannot
supply the missing target result. The full-support receipt remains a
historical partial observation; the scalar receipt is a terminal failure
of its original invocation. Neither is a replay of the subsequently
repaired source configuration.

This editorial revision does not establish a new formal result.
Detailed reading coverage, exact finite-check
results, preserved unsuccessful observations and the remaining obligations
are recorded in the companion source review. This remains a draft after source-based agent review; independent mathematical acceptance and a human reconstruction study have not been performed.
